label: doc_title
text: LOSS OF “VALERIAN.”

label: paragraph_title
text: Commander's Striking Account.

label: paragraph_title
text: NAVAL TRADITIONS UPHELD.

label: paragraph_title
text:
Series of Squalls Beggar
Description.

label: text
text: A stirring account of the sinking of the British Naval sloop "Valerian" was given by Commander Usher at the court-martial to enquire into the loss of the ship which honourably acquitted all the nineteen survivors. It found that every one was at his post until the first, and that all had maintained British Naval traditions by exemplary conduct.

label: paragraph_title
text: Störm.Warning.

label: text
text: Commander Usher reported that economical steaming was necessary on sailing from the Bahamas, owing to the scarcity of bunkers. He received warnings when 200 miles from Bermuda, so he increased his speed to a maximum of 9½ knots with one boiler. Further warnings led him to start a second boiler, and increase the steaming rate to 11½ knots, but he slowed down to 10 knots owing to the bearings becoming heated. He was only five miles from Gibbs Hill at eight o'clock in the morning; but, contrary to anticipation, was unable to make land and headed for the south-east.

label: text
text: The wind increased and, thundis capped with the maximum engine power at her disposal, the ship was seaworthy until one afternoon when a series of squalls, begging description, ensued. The "Valerian" healed over 70 degrees, but righted herself again. More squalls followed and the engines stopped. The ship was apparently aground, though no breakers were visible. She turned over and slowly her funnels became submerged; her boilers exploded; and she sank.

label: paragraph_title
text: Men Take to Rafts:

label: text
text: The men boarded rafts which tossed about and were turned over day and night until the warship "Capetown" arrived at ten o'clock on the following morning just when the exhausted survivors were beginning to lose hold.

label: text
text:
Twelve out 28 were saved on the
ommander's raft.

label: text
text: The survivors say that Commander Usher sank with his ship, clinging to the bridge, but was washed off and caught hold of a raft.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: President in Train Smash

label: text
text: Northampton (Massachusetts), Nov. 2.

label: text
text:
President Coolidge and his wife arrived and proceeded to the polls to record their votes. They will return forthwith to Washington.
An exciting incident occurred near Baltimore when the President's train crashed into a motor car in which were two soldiers. The latter escaped uninjured. The impact, however, caused the front wheels of the engine to jump. President Coolidge was asleep at the time and was awakened by the shock.—Reuter's American Service.

label: paragraph_title
text: PLOT IN SPAIN.

label: text
text: NUPPED IN BUDD BY THE POLICE

label: text
text: SIXTY ARRESTS.

label: text
text: Perpignan; Nov. 2

label: text
text:
What is believed to be an extensive revolutionary plot directed against Spain was nipped in the bud by the prompt action of the Police in arresting about 60 persons at various points of the frontier who, it is alleged, furnished field telephones and military equipment to Spanish Italian, and British subjects disguised as tourists.
The suspicions of the French authorities were aroused by the despatch of numerous cipher telegrams.

label: text
text: The frontier trains were closely scrutinised, resulting in widespread arrests unearthing the conspiracy whereby the revolutionaries were supposed to have arranged to assemble at Estagell, Bataille, and Milhas, and thence proceed across the frontier and launch a revolution.—Reuter.

label: text
text: The newspapers deny that there is any foundation for the recent "disquieting rumours." The "Nacion" says that the Government cannot be blamed for taking any necessary measures for the security of the State.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: WORK OF CONFERENCE COMMITTEES.

label: text
text: INDUSTRIAL STANDARDS.

label: paragraph_title
text: Rugby, November 2.

label: text
text: A detailed examination by the Imperial Conference of the work of the Navy Army and Air Force was completed to-day when the delegates visited the Air Ministry.

label: text
text: At a full meeting of the Conference on Thursday the general aspects of the Empire defence problem will be resumed.

label: text
text: "This afternoon the Committee of Prime Ministers further considered questions affecting inter-Imperial relations."

label: text
text: Several of the special Committee also met.

label: text
text: The Overseas Settlement Committee devoted itself mainly to migration questions affecting Australia.

label: text
text:
The Research Sub-Committee was engaged in considering machinery for organisation which would enable different parts of the Empire to reap full advantage of the results achieved by research work elsewhere in the Empire.
The Economic Committee completed its investigation of the question of industrial standardisation within the Empire. A report has been prepared on the proposal that some authoritative body or bodies should determine the essential dimensions, materials, and qualities of manufactured products, and the adoption by users generally of the specifications thus laid down. The survey of the whole question revealed that much had already been effected in this matter in the Mother Country and the Dominions—in South Africa, the numbers of types of engines in use on the railways have, as a result, been reduced in 16 years from 68 to 11—but it was generally agreed that much remains to be done—British Wireless Service

label: paragraph_title
text: LABOUR TIDE

label: text
text: SWEEPING GAINS IN ELECTIONS

label: text
text: Rugby, Nov. 2.

label: text
text: The latest results of the municipal elections in England and Wales show that the Labour Party has a net gain of 147 seats. The Conservatives have a net loss of 70 seats, the Liberals a net loss of 49, and the Independents a net loss of 21.

label: text
text:
London is not involved in these elections. Its municipal elections are held only every three years, whereas in the provinces elections take place each year for one-third of the members of the Councils.
Labour circles express the greatest satisfaction with the results of the elections.—British Wireless Service.

Dorlot, the Communist Deputy, was present, a stranger brought “salutations from the Communists of Russia,” saying: “I have no right to be in France, but I care nothing for the French police.” At Lille railway station, after the meeting, the stranger admitted to a Commissioner of Police who had followed him that he had entered France with a false passport. At the police station, a considerable sum of money in dollars and pounds sterling was found in his possession. He was conducted over the frontier.
